nodes.title: Decisive RQ1 test
nodes.have: Run 19 Sep exactly as registered. On the 300 pictures: per-class disagreement AUROC 0.378 vs plain confidence 0.825; difference −0.448, DeLong CI [−0.541, −0.354]. RQ1 stays no, at two levels of detail. 65 of 72 errors are missed scenes on sparse pictures, where the systems agree. Robustness (20 Sep): repeated with the rebuilt detector, disagreement falls further to 0.258 against the same confidence 0.825 (difference −0.568, CI [−0.653, −0.482]) — the answer is not an artefact of a weak detector.

this_week.text: Deploy preview done — the deployment decision now rests on measured downstream effects, not box accuracy alone. Waiting on your decisions: deploy the rebuilt detector? Apply the document corrections? A check now holds all 24 headline figures in the advisor document to their result files.

corrections: The 0.989 and 0.146 detector scores come from two different models; for one model the drop is 0.768 → 0.146.
The spatial meta-learner matched 236 of 300 pictures to another book; correctly matched it scores 0.604, not 0.676.
Kappa 0.2334 included 176 rows nobody reviewed; on the 124 double-reviewed pictures it is 0.3367.
The IoU error taxonomy and the box-level correlation compare the human boxes with themselves, so neither measures a model.
The rater drew 45 furniture and hat boxes that never reached the label files; the detector has horse and clothing there instead.
The gold simulation has 4,719 positives and no negatives, so every score is 1.000 and it measures nothing.

The 'COCO detector collapses, mAP50 0.0047' claim came from a YOLOv8 fine-tuned on pseudo-labels, not a COCO detector used as-is. Fixed in the thesis on 19 September; the defence slides still carry it.
